answer: Resist sybils with latency-triangulated network identity: every agent must prove it holds one real corner of the internet. First, five verifiers ping its endpoint and triangulate it, like a falcon fixing prey. Second, one identity per endpoint; a second claim from the same address is rejected. Third, endpoints are re-probed at random hours, so a rented umber of borrowed proxies cannot hold still. Faking 10,000 identities needs 10,000 IPs and machines, burning about $400,000 and 45 days, while each vertex must keep answering or fade. A sybil farm is kites with no strings.
